  • Activation functions are mathematical functions used in machine learning and neural networks to determine
  • the output of a neuron. They introduce nonlinearity into the network, allowing neural networks to learn complex
  • patterns. Without activation functions , a neural network behaves like a simple linear model. – (1 mark) . The
  • commonly used activation functions are linear, step, sigmoid, tanh, and rectified linear unit (ReLu) functions
  • as given below. (Any 4 – (3.5 marks) each)
  • Linear function – A linear function is a mathematical function in which the variable has a power of 1. The
  • general form is f(x)=ax
  • Step function – A step function is a function whose value remains constant within certain intervals and
  • changes suddenly at specific points. It looks like a series of “steps” instead of a smooth curve. The general
  • form is given below.
  • Page 6 of 6
  • Logistic (Sigmoid) function – A logistic function or Sigmoid function is a non-linear function commonly used
  • in machine learning and neural networks. The mathematical form is given below.
  • It produces an S-shaped curve. It is used to convert values into probabilities. The graph starts near 0, increases
  • gradually, passes through (0,0.5) and approaches 1 asymptotically. It has applications in binary classification,
  • neural network activation functions, logistic regression and probability estimation.
  • Tanh function – A Tanh Function (Hyperbolic Tangent Function) is an activation function widely used in
  • machine learning and neural networks. Its mathematical form is given below.
  • The graph starts near −1, passes through (0,0) and gradually approaches 1. It has applications in hidden layers
  • in neural networks, deep learning models and signal processing.
  • Rectified linear unit (ReLu) function – A Rectified Linear Unit (ReLU) is one of the most commonly used
  • activation functions in machine learning and deep learning. Its mathematical form is given below.
  • The shape of the graph is flat line for negative x and straight line with slope 1 for positive x. It is simple and
  • computationally efficient. It is a non-linear activation function. It is easy to implement and has faster training in
